niche_preference_profile: This user prefers clean, airy, well-structured interfaces that feel finished and functional. They like light backgrounds, clear hierarchy, concise labels, and layouts that are either spacious and minimal or, when the task is a settings/list screen, sufficiently populated to feel complete. They favor simple, direct controls, strong but restrained primary actions, and screens that avoid visual clutter, awkward empty space, or overly aggressive alert styling.

criteria.description: Prefers light, airy, clean backgrounds over dark, heavy ones.
Prefers strong visual hierarchy with prominent titles, clear section structure, and obvious grouping.
Prefers short, direct, easy-to-scan copy over wordy or explanatory text.
Prefers screens that look complete, production-ready, and fully populated rather than placeholder-like or unfinished.
Prefers straightforward controls such as simple toggles, clear buttons, and obvious actions over complex or multi-state interactions.
Prefers primary actions that are clearly visible and assertive without feeling harsh, alarming, or overly loud.
Prefers interfaces with low visual clutter, fewer competing elements, and a calm overall composition.
Prefers layouts with balanced spacing and breathing room rather than awkward empty zones or cramped stacking.
Prefers content organized into distinct, understandable sections or cards with clear boundaries and labels.
Prefers screens that present a focused set of relevant options instead of broad, mixed, or overly expansive settings.
Prefers simple, clean surfaces and subtle separators over heavy card contrast or overly decorative framing.
Prefers UI states to be explicit and legible, including disabled states, selected states, and empty vs populated states.
Prefers labels and headings that are specific, concrete, and immediately informative.
Prefers warning and alert screens that feel serious, controlled, and reassuring rather than aggressive or punitive.
Prefers modal dialogs that strongly isolate the focal content from the background and minimize surrounding distractions.
On management/list screens, prefers populated lists with visible item details and per-item actions rather than empty or sparse states.
Prefers compact, well-contained card modules with clean spacing over oversized or awkwardly emphasized panels.
Prefers a friendly, approachable product tone when the screen is onboarding or guidance-oriented.
